title: Measurability of the Mills integrand
statement: Let $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian density, and define $H:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by $H(x)=\varphi(x)(1-3(x^4)^{-1})$ for every real $x$, with $0^{-1}=0$. Then $H$ is measurable.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, and define $H:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by $H(0)=\varphi(0)$ and $H(x)=\varphi(x)(1-3x^{-4})$ for $x\ne0$. The function $H$ is Borel measurable.
